text:
maya: Heads up — we just saw a sharp 99th pct spike on inference for eu-west1-rack10 around 09:23 UTC. Throughput dipped for ~30s repeatedly over the last 10m. Looks like a GPU-level clock reset.

alex: On which host? any Xid/ECC in logs?

maya: node=rack10-gpu-12. quick grep in /var/log/syslog shows repeated kernel messages. paste below.

maya: ```
Sep 12 09:22:47 rack10-gpu-12 kernel: NVRM: GPU 0000:3b:00.0: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 31, PID=0, GPU has fallen off the bus.
Sep 12 09:22:47 rack10-gpu-12 kernel: nvidia: OEM power management: PCIe link state change
Sep 12 09:22:47 rack10-gpu-12 kernel: EDAC MC0: ECC error detected in memory scrub, corrected single-bit error
Sep 12 09:22:48 rack10-gpu-12 kernel: NVRM: GPU 0000:3b:00.0: GPU rebooted due to Xid 31
```

sam: Xid 31 + corrected ECC singles — could be memory scrubbing triggered by a voltage sag or thermal transient. Any correlating BMC/PSU logs?

infra-bot: Alert: inference-99th-latency spike on service=embedder, hosts affected: rack10-gpu-{11,12}, started=2026-09-12T09:22:45Z

alex: Maya — can you post recent `nvidia-smi` snapshot and NVML traces if available? Also NV switch logs.

maya: grabbing `nvidia-smi -q` output now. short snippet: 

maya: ```
GPU 0: Tesla-A100
    Power Draw                      : 243.65 W
    Power Limit                     : 255.00 W
    Clocks                            : Graphics 1095 MHz, Memory 877 MHz
    Persistence Mode                : Enabled
    Retired Pages                   : 0
```

maya: But right before the reset the kernel shows clocks dropping then device disconnect. Not consistent with steady thermal plateau. temps are ~72C.

jordan: Could be PCIe link retrain / ASPM negotiation on the host side causing transient loss-of-communication, NV driver triggers GPU reset -> Xid 31. Have we seen any PMIC/12V rail dips on the BMC?

maya: BMC shows a momentary 12V rail dip on PSU1 at 09:22:47 for 200-300ms. PSU2 steady. Logs: `psu-monitor: rail12_drop duration=230ms source=psu1 voltage=11.3V`

sam: That aligns. Short rail hiccup -> ECC scrub -> corrected ECC + Xid recovery. If the driver loses link during a scrub that could force a reset.

alex: Immediate mitigation: isolate the GPU from noisy policy that toggles boost/auto-power, and set a fixed power cap and persistence mode. Commands: 

alex: ```
# enable persistence + set power limit
nvidia-smi -i 0 -pm 1
nvidia-smi -i 0 -pl 240
# pin clocks lower until we confirm stability
nvidia-smi -i 0 -lgc 800,1200
```

maya: applied -pm 1 and -pl 240 on rack10-gpu-12 a few mins ago. Observing.

infra-bot: Runbook note: ticket created INFRA-2421 for hardware triage (owner=sam).

sam: Next steps I'm proposing: 1) cordon/drain node from k8s on a gradual window to avoid waterfall impact 2) repro with stress-ng memtester in isolated maintenance to see if ECCs increase 3) swap PSU1 if we can reproduce 4) if GPU continues flaking after PSU swap, RMA card.

jordan: Also suggest flipping off PCIe ASPM in BIOS for that host temporarily; ASPM can cause link power state transitions that some combos don't handle gracefully.

alex: Agree. For immediate safety, let's drain the node from serving and move workloads to rack10-gpu-11. Maya — can you schedule a drain in the next 5m? 

maya: draining now: `kubectl drain rack10-gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60` — moving pods over.

maya: done. traffic rerouted. embedder 99p back to normal for now (watching).

sam: I'm going to repro in maintenance: memtester 1G x 4 + synthetic GPU load for 10m while we monitor BMC/psu/driver. Will log nvml traces.

sam: quick note — I saw a slightly older log entry from this machine last month about a fan PWM jitter; might be related to PSU cable seating. I'll do a physical check during swap.

jordan: If PSUs are redundant but not load-balanced the failing one can still create micro-sags during peak bursts. Good catch.

maya: after setting power cap we haven't seen further Xid in the last 8m. latency stable.

infra-bot: Update: INFRA-2421 status=investigating, assignee=sam, priority=high

alex: One more ask — add a short Prom alert for Xid>0 rate per host for future early detection. Current metric set is per-cluster only.

maya: filing alert rule now. linking to ticket.

sam: I'll attempt repro now. I'll attach NVML trace and BMC logs to INFRA-2421. If the memtester causes ECC singles to spike correlated with PSU dips, plan is PSU replacement then stress rerun. If no PSU evidence, next is PCIe riser/cable and BIOS ASPM off.

maya: thanks all. assigning follow-ups: sam=hardware triage, alex=alert + runbook update, jordan=bios change approval for host, maya=traffic migration and monitoring.

alex: :thumbsup: Keep thread updated. If we get >1 Xid in 24h on same card we treat as immediate RMA candidate.

jordan: Also add a note to fleet dashboard about recent PSU firmware on this batch; there was a vendor fw push last quarter that changed power reporting behavior. could be related.

maya: logging that. will circle back after sam's repro.

sam: repro done — memtester + GPU load ran for 15m. Observed one ECC corrected single-bit at 09:54, and BMC recorded a 150ms 12V dip again. No Xid this run. attaching logs to ticket.

maya: marking node unschedulable for now until PSU swap.

infra-bot: INFRA-2421 updated: hardware-swap scheduled 2026-09-13T02:30Z (PSU1 replacement)

maya: closing loop: after PSU swap and run of 1h stress the card stabilized. will keep node in degraded pool for 48h and monitor.

alex: Great. Postmortem if we see recurrence. For now leave the new alert enabled and add a dashboard widget for short 12V rail drops per host.

maya: will do.

jordan: thanks team.

maya: :white_check_mark:
